problems.title: A rational sign chart
problems.question: Solve [(x−6)⁶(x²−8x+15)(x−2)⁴]/[(x−7)⁵(x²−5x+4)(x²−4x+4)]≥0.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Factor the quadratics; exclude x=1,2,4,7. The sign away from zeros is (x−3)(x−5)/[(x−7)(x−1)(x−4)].
steps: The sign is positive on (1,3),(4,5),(7,∞). Include numerator zeros 3 and 5.
The even-power zero x=6 is an additional allowed point. The canceled point 2 remains excluded.

problems.title: Exactly one of three visas
problems.question: The visa probabilities for the USA, Canada, Mexico are 0.3,0.5,0.9. Find the probability of receiving exactly one.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Under independence, sum three disjoint cases.
problems.answer: 0.365 if the visa outcomes are independent.
problems.note: Independence is not stated in the problem. The three marginal probabilities alone do not determine the probability of exactly one visa.

problems.title: Height of a cyclic trapezoid from its area
problems.question: A cyclic trapezoid has area 108. A leg subtends central angle α, with tan(α/2)=3/4. Find the height.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: For an isosceles cyclic trapezoid, h/m=tan(α/2), where m is the midline.
steps: Then h=9. The identity follows by joining the center to the leg endpoints and using symmetry of the parallel chords.

problems.title: Prove a power inequality
problems.question: Prove 199ⁿ>41ⁿ+42ⁿ for every natural n≥1.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: Since 199>83>0, raising to positive integer n gives 199ⁿ>83ⁿ.
Combine the inequalities, retaining the strict first one.

problems.title: Width of an equal-area ring
problems.question: A circle of radius √10(√7+√6) is divided by nine concentric circles into ten equal-area regions. Find the width between circles six and seven, counted outward.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The kth circle has radius rₖ=R√(k/10).

problems.title: An inconsistent progression statement
problems.question: Four numbers form an arithmetic progression. Subtract respectively 5,11,13,3; the printed question says the results also form an arithmetic progression. Find the numbers.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Subtracting two arithmetic progressions must yield an arithmetic progression.
steps: The fixed subtractions would have to be an arithmetic progression. Their successive differences are 6,2,−10, which are unequal.
Equivalently, if original difference is d, the new differences are d−6,d−2,d+10 and cannot all agree.
problems.note: The source PDF says arithmetic progression for both sets. Some transcriptions say geometric for the second set; that is a different problem.
